meta.title: Lexis: Meaning & Word Formation
meta.randomizationRule: Randomize question selection/order and answer-option order on every attempt; never reuse an exact attempt signature.
meta.alignment: TKT Module 1 — Describing language: Lexis — types of meaning and word formation
meta.scopeNote: Synonyms, antonyms, lexical sets, homophones, collocation and register are intentionally reserved for Unit 4.

questions.stem: In the word “unhelpful”, both “un-” and “-ful” change or add to the meaning of the base word “help”.
questions.explanation: An affix is a meaningful group of letters added to the beginning or end of a root or base word.

questions.stem: The words “reusable” and “careless” contain meaningful elements added to a base word.
questions.prompt: Which term describes these added elements in general?
questions.explanation: Prefixes and suffixes are both types of affix.

questions.stem: Which pair consists entirely of affixes?
questions.explanation: “Un-” is a prefix and “-ness” is a suffix, so both are affixes.

questions.stem: In the word “disagree”, “dis-” is added before the base word “agree”.
questions.explanation: A prefix is an affix added to the beginning of a root or base word.

questions.stem: Which word contains a prefix?
questions.explanation: “Re-” is added before “write”, so it is a prefix.

questions.stem: What does the prefix “un-” do in the word “unfriendly”?
options: It changes the meaning of the base word
questions.correctAnswer: It changes the meaning of the base word
questions.explanation: A prefix can modify the meaning of a root or base word. Here “un-” gives the opposite or negative meaning.

questions.stem: In the word “teacher”, “-er” is added to the end of “teach”.
questions.explanation: A suffix is an affix added to the end of a root or base word.

questions.stem: Which word contains a suffix that changes a verb into a noun referring to a person?
questions.explanation: The suffix “-er” is added to the verb “write” to form the noun “writer”.

questions.stem: In “careful”, what does “-ful” represent?
questions.explanation: “-ful” is added after the base word “care”, so it is a suffix.

questions.stem: The words “helpful”, “helpless” and “unhelpful” are all formed from “help”.
questions.explanation: A root or base word is the basic word or part from which other words can be formed.

questions.stem: What is the base word in “disagreement”?
questions.explanation: “Agree” is the base word. “Dis-” and “-ment” are affixes added to it.

questions.stem: Which word is the root/base for “photographer” and “photographic”?
questions.explanation: “Photograph” is the base from which “photographer” and “photographic” are formed.

questions.stem: The word “whiteboard” combines “white” and “board” to make one lexical item.
questions.prompt: What type of lexical item is “whiteboard”?
questions.explanation: A compound is made from two or more words that function together as one unit of meaning.

questions.stem: Which item is a compound?
questions.explanation: “Textbook” combines “text” and “book” into one lexical item.

questions.stem: Which example is a compound adjective?
questions.explanation: “Well-known” combines two elements that function together as one adjective.

questions.stem: educate – education – educational – educator
questions.explanation: A word family is a group of words related through the same root or base word.

questions.stem: Which group is a word family?
questions.explanation: These words share the same root and are related by word formation.

questions.stem: Why are “employ”, “employee” and “employment” considered a word family?
options: They all have exactly the same meaning
questions.explanation: Members of a word family are related through a shared root or base word.

questions.stem: A Spanish learner thinks English “actually” means Spanish “actual” (= current), although “actually” means “in fact”.
questions.prompt: What lexical term describes this problem?
questions.explanation: A false friend is a target-language word that looks or sounds similar to an L1 word but has a different meaning.

questions.stem: A learner assumes that a familiar-looking word in English has the same meaning as a similar word in their first language, but it does not.
questions.prompt: What is the English word called?
questions.explanation: False friends can mislead learners because similarity of form does not guarantee similarity of meaning.

questions.stem: Which situation best illustrates a false friend?
options: A learner gives an English word the meaning of a similar-looking L1 word when the meanings differ
A learner confuses two English words that sound the same
questions.correctAnswer: A learner gives an English word the meaning of a similar-looking L1 word when the meanings differ
questions.explanation: False friends involve misleading similarity between a target-language word and a word in the learner's first language.

questions.stem: The noun “bank” can refer to a financial institution or the side of a river.
questions.prompt: What lexical term describes these different meanings of the same word form?
questions.explanation: Homonyms share the same form but have different meanings.

questions.stem: Which example best illustrates homonymy?
options: bat = an animal / bat = equipment used in sport
questions.correctAnswer: bat = an animal / bat = equipment used in sport
questions.explanation: The same word form “bat” has two distinct meanings.

questions.stem: A learner sees the word “match” in two texts: one refers to a sports event and the other to a small stick used to make fire.
questions.explanation: The same written word form can represent distinct meanings.

questions.stem: After the interview, Maya said, “It was a piece of cake.” She meant it was very easy.
questions.prompt: What type of lexical item is “a piece of cake” in this use?
questions.explanation: An idiom is a fixed or semi-fixed group whose overall meaning is not simply the meaning of the individual words.

questions.stem: Which expression is being used idiomatically?
options: break the ice = make people feel more relaxed
open the window = move the window so air can enter
write the answer = put the answer on paper
questions.correctAnswer: break the ice = make people feel more relaxed
questions.explanation: The figurative meaning of “break the ice” is different from the literal meanings of the individual words.

questions.stem: Why can idioms be difficult for learners?
options: The overall meaning may not be predictable from the individual words
questions.correctAnswer: The overall meaning may not be predictable from the individual words
questions.explanation: Understanding each word separately may not reveal the idiom's intended meaning.

questions.stem: Please “look up” the new term in the glossary.
questions.prompt: What type of lexical item is “look up”?
questions.explanation: A phrasal verb contains a verb plus a particle or preposition and functions as one lexical unit.

questions.stem: Which item is a phrasal verb?
questions.explanation: “Give up” consists of a verb plus a particle and has a lexical meaning as a unit.

questions.stem: In “The meeting was called off”, what does “called off” illustrate?
questions.explanation: “Call off” is a multi-word verb meaning to cancel.

questions.stem: Which statement about an affix is correct?
options: It is added to a root or base word
It must always be a complete word
It is another term for an idiom
questions.correctAnswer: It is added to a root or base word
questions.explanation: Affixes are meaningful elements added to roots or base words.

questions.stem: Which word contains both a prefix and a suffix?
questions.explanation: “Unhappiness” contains the prefix “un-” and the suffix “-ness” around the base “happy”.

questions.stem: Which pair shows two different kinds of affix?
questions.explanation: “Re-” is a prefix and “-able” is a suffix; both are affixes.

questions.stem: In “misunderstand”, which element is the prefix?
questions.explanation: A prefix occurs before a root or base word; “mis-” is added before “understand”.

questions.stem: Which word is formed by adding a prefix to a base word?
questions.explanation: “Im-” is a prefix added to the base adjective “possible”.

questions.stem: What is the function of “re-” in “reconsider”?
options: It is a prefix that adds meaning to the base verb
It is a suffix that changes the word class
It creates a compound from two independent words
questions.correctAnswer: It is a prefix that adds meaning to the base verb
questions.explanation: “Re-” occurs before “consider” and typically adds the meaning of doing something again.

questions.stem: Which element is the suffix in “development”?
questions.explanation: “-ment” is added to the end of the base verb “develop”.

questions.stem: Which word contains a suffix that changes an adjective into a noun?
questions.explanation: The suffix “-ness” changes the adjective “kind” into the noun “kindness”.

questions.stem: What is “-less” in the word “careless”?
questions.explanation: “-less” is attached to the end of the base word “care”.

questions.stem: What is the base word in “unpredictable”?
questions.explanation: “Predict” is the base. The prefix “un-” and suffix “-able” are added around it.

questions.stem: Which statement best defines a root or base word?
options: A basic form from which related words can be created
A group of unrelated words on the same topic
A word with two unrelated meanings
questions.correctAnswer: A basic form from which related words can be created
questions.explanation: Roots or base words provide the form from which related words may be built.

questions.stem: Which item is the base for “successful”, “successfully” and “unsuccessful”?
questions.explanation: “Success” is the common base used to form the related words.

questions.stem: Which item is a compound noun?
questions.explanation: “Lesson plan” combines two words that function together as one lexical unit.

questions.stem: Which item is NOT formed by affixation?
questions.explanation: “Classroom” is a compound made from “class” + “room”; it is not created by adding an affix.

questions.stem: Which description best fits a compound?
options: Two or more words functioning as one unit of meaning
A letter group added only to the end of a word
Two words that sound the same
questions.correctAnswer: Two or more words functioning as one unit of meaning
questions.explanation: Compounds are built from multiple words or word elements that function together as a lexical unit.

questions.stem: Which set forms a word family?
questions.explanation: These forms share a common root and are related through word formation.

questions.stem: A teacher groups “produce”, “producer”, “production” and “productive” together.
questions.prompt: Which lexical concept is the teacher illustrating?
questions.explanation: The words are related by a shared root/base and different word-building processes.

questions.stem: Which feature is essential to a word family?
options: A shared root or base word
Exactly the same part of speech
questions.correctAnswer: A shared root or base word
questions.explanation: Word-family members are connected through a common root or base; their word classes and forms may differ.

questions.stem: An English learner sees a target-language word that resembles an L1 word and assumes the meanings are identical, but they are not.
questions.explanation: A false friend creates misleading cross-language similarity in form or sound.

questions.stem: Spanish “embarazada” means “pregnant”, not English “embarrassed”. This pair is commonly used to illustrate which lexical concept?
questions.explanation: The words look similar across the two languages but their meanings differ.

questions.stem: Which feature distinguishes a false friend from a homonym?
options: A false friend involves misleading similarity across languages
A false friend must be a multi-word verb
A false friend is formed by adding a suffix
questions.correctAnswer: A false friend involves misleading similarity across languages
questions.explanation: False friends concern target-language forms that resemble L1 forms but differ in meaning; homonyms are forms within a language with distinct meanings.

questions.stem: The word “light” can refer to illumination or mean “not heavy”.
questions.prompt: Which term best describes this lexical relationship?
questions.explanation: The same word form is associated with different meanings.

questions.stem: Which example best represents homonyms?
options: seal = an animal / seal = close something tightly
questions.correctAnswer: seal = an animal / seal = close something tightly
questions.explanation: “Seal” has the same form but distinct meanings.

questions.stem: A dictionary gives separate meanings for the same spelling “file”: a folder for documents and a metal tool for smoothing a surface.
questions.explanation: The same written form represents distinct lexical meanings.

questions.stem: “Hit the books” means “study hard”.
questions.prompt: What type of expression is this?
questions.explanation: The overall meaning is not obtained simply by interpreting “hit” and “books” literally.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an idiom?
options: Its overall meaning may differ from the literal meanings of its individual words
It always contains a prefix and a suffix
It is always a formal expression
questions.correctAnswer: Its overall meaning may differ from the literal meanings of its individual words
questions.explanation: Idioms function as lexical units whose meanings are often non-literal.

questions.stem: In “We need to get the ball rolling”, the speaker means “We need to start the process.”
questions.prompt: Which term describes “get the ball rolling”?
questions.explanation: The phrase has a conventional non-literal meaning as a whole.

questions.stem: The teacher asked the learners to “find out” the meaning from context.
questions.explanation: “Find out” is a verb plus particle functioning together as a multi-word verb.

questions.stem: Which sentence contains a phrasal verb?
questions.explanation: “Hand in” is a multi-word verb meaning to submit something.

questions.stem: Why is it useful to treat “put off” as one lexical unit in “They put off the meeting”?
options: Its combined meaning is “postpone”, which is not obtained by interpreting each word separately
questions.correctAnswer: Its combined meaning is “postpone”, which is not obtained by interpreting each word separately
questions.explanation: Phrasal verbs often have a meaning that belongs to the combination as a whole.
